ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the two banks of the river are parallel to each other, and the water flow velocity is constant and unchanged. When the boat travels, the magnitude of its velocity relative to the water is always unchanged. At first, the boat sets out from point A on the bank, with the boat body always perpendicular to the riverbank, and the boat happens to arrive at point B on the opposite bank along route AB, taking time t1; the angle between AB and the riverbank is 60°. Adjusting the direction of the boat speed, it sets out from point B and returns along the straight line BA back to point A, taking time t2. Then t1∶t2 is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the two banks of the river are drawn as two horizontal straight lines parallel to each other; point A is on the lower bank, and point B is on the upper bank and located to the upper right of A; the connecting line AB is an oblique line, and near A the angle between AB and the riverbank is marked as 60°; there is also an arrow pointing to the right in the river, indicating that the water flow direction is to the right. Reasoning: Let the magnitude of the water flow velocity be v, with direction to the right; the magnitude of the boat's velocity relative to the water is constantly u. On the outbound trip A→B, the boat body is always perpendicular to the riverbank, and according to the problem statement the direction of the boat's velocity relative to the water is perpendicular to the riverbank, that is, vertically upward. Therefore the horizontal component of the boat's ground velocity is v, the vertical component is u, and the resultant velocity is along the direction AB. Since the angle between AB and the riverbank is 60°, u/v = tan60° = √3, so u = √3v. The magnitude of the outbound ground velocity is √(v²+u²)=√(v²+3v²)=2v. On the return trip B→A, the boat returns along the straight line BA. Let the magnitude of the return ground velocity be k, with direction along BA, that is, toward the lower left, and the angle with the horizontal riverbank is still 60°, so its components are (-k cos60°, -k sin60°)=(-k/2, -√3k/2). The boat's velocity relative to the water equals the ground velocity minus the water flow velocity, with components (-k/2-v, -√3k/2), and its magnitude is still equal to u=√3v. Thus (k/2+v)²+(√3k/2)²=3v², which simplifies to k²+kv-2v²=0; taking the positive root gives k=v. The distances traveled in the two trips are both AB, so t1=AB/(2v), t2=AB/v, therefore t1:t2=1:2.
